objective.value: Characterize E. coli transcript 3'-ends (T3PEs) genome-wide using Term-Seq plus machine learning to build a tunable collection of 3'-UTR/Rho-independent terminator bioparts, and apply them as synthetic 3'-UTR 'metabolic valves' to optimally balance flux between heterologous product pathways (2,3-butanediol from acetoin; myo-inositol production) and endogenous metabolism in E. coli.
objective.notes: Two-tier objective: (1) discovery/characterization of terminator bioparts (platform), (2) application to metabolic flux control (engineering demonstration).

hypothesis.value: 3'-UTR terminator bioparts with graded transcription-termination strengths can modulate gene expression without trans-acting elements and with lower noise than inducible-promoter control, and inserting terminators of graded strength between pathway genes can tune the split of metabolic flux to maximize target-product titer; the optimal flux split differs between host strains.
hypothesis.notes: Partly stated as authors' framing in Abstract/Introduction; the host-dependent-optimum part is supported by Results (MG1655 vs eMS57 MI experiments).

experiments.purpose: Compare expression noise of terminator-biopart architecture vs conventional dual-promoter regulation
experiments.intervention: pDRA2 DualP (araC-araBAD cassette added to drive RFP independently) as dual-promoter reference vs single-promoter terminator-biopart pDRA2
experiments.conditions: M9 glucose, 24 h, 37°C; IPTG 1/10 µM; L-arabinose 1/10/30 mM
experiments.control: dual-promoter system as conventional reference architecture
experiments.readout: Dual-promoter: η_ext 0.451, η_int 18.4, η_tot 18.4; terminator system: η_int 4.08-fold lower, η_tot 4.07-fold lower, η_ext ~unchanged (1.04×)
experiments.analysis: CV decomposition via scatter rotation along regression slope
experiments.outcome: Terminator bioparts give ~4.1-fold lower total noise by removing transcription-initiation/TF sources of intrinsic variation

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: authors designed and built the terminator-biopart single-promoter architecture (and the DualP reference) as a low-noise alternative to promoter/RBS-based control. Q2 pass: constructed in this paper. Q3 pass: the noise advantage is a stated design rule supporting use of terminator valves in downstream pathway constructs.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Choice of regulatory architecture (3'-UTR terminator instead of additional promoter/RBS) to balance expression of multiple genes from one transcript with low noise - an expression-balancing action.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Promoter/5'-UTR control requires precious inducer molecules and introduces noise via trans-acting elements (Introduction); goal of reducing genetic-circuit complexity.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Direct single-cell flow-cytometry noise measurements of both architectures in this study.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives an explicit mechanistic rationale: removing trans-acting elements and RNAP/TF initiation events reduces intrinsic noise sources (η_int), consistent with measured decomposition.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When balancing multi-gene expression in E. coli synthetic pathways where inducer cost and expression noise must be minimized, apply a single promoter with 3'-UTR terminator bioparts of graded strength instead of multiple inducible promoters, because terminator control removes trans-acting-element-dependent initiation noise (≈4-fold lower intrinsic noise) while retaining tunable relative expression.
alternatives_considered: conventional dual-promoter (lac + araBAD) system - higher intrinsic noise (η_int 18.4)

experiments.purpose: Demonstrate terminator 'metabolic valve' control of the acetoin → 2,3-BDO branch
experiments.intervention: pBDO plasmids: alsS(B. subtilis)-alsD(A. hydrophila)-[RIT valve]-bdh(T. brockii, codon-optimized); three RIT groups (A: read-through <1, 5 RITs; B: read-through >1, 4 RITs; C: 3 short-half-life RITs) + empty
experiments.conditions: 60 mL M9 high-glucose (10 g/L) + 100 µg/mL amp + 0.1 mM IPTG, OD600 0.05, 300 mL flask, 37°C, 24 h, aerobic
experiments.control: pBDO empty (fully induced, no termination) as negative control; pBDO rrnBT strong-termination reference
experiments.readout: HPLC titers of acetoin and 2,3-BDO at 24 h: rrnBT 0.126 g/L BDO; empty 0.382 g/L; Group B max 0.513 g/L; plateau at read-through 2.343 (T3PE-390); Group C lowest
experiments.analysis: BDO:acetoin ratio logarithmically proportional to T3PE read-through (Suppl. Fig S8)
experiments.outcome: Terminators quantitatively valve flux between acetoin and 2,3-BDO; read-through >1 Group B elements exceed no-terminator expression (attributed by authors to post-transcriptional processing exposing RBS; 5/13 Group B showed stable 5'-ends by dRNA-Seq)

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: deliberate insertion of selected RITs between alsSD and bdh to set bdh expression and flux split. Q2 pass: pBDO valve series constructed in this paper. Q3 pass: results established the read-through-to-flux-split relationship used to select valves (and carried into the MI system).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Balancing relative expression of pathway genes (alsSD vs bdh) via intergenic terminator strength to redistribute flux between two products.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: RITs characterized by pDRA1/pDRA2 span a wide quantitative read-through range (0.004-91.4), providing a parts basis for graded downstream-gene control without extra promoters.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured extracellular titers (HPLC) across the valve series plus prior measured read-through values; the Group B processing explanation (RBS exposure after cleavage) is supported by dRNA-Seq for 5/13 but remains partly inferential.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The valve mechanism (partial termination sets transcript ratio of upstream vs downstream cistrons) is mechanistically explicit in the paper; the Group B 'processing exposes RBS' sub-explanation is author interpretation supported by 5'-end mapping of a subset.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When tuning flux split between two consecutive products of a branched heterologous pathway in E. coli (validated for acetoin/2,3-BDO from pyruvate), apply an intercistronic Rho-independent terminator of chosen read-through strength to set downstream-enzyme expression, because the product ratio scales logarithmically with terminator read-through, allowing single-promoter, inducer-free pathway balancing.
alternatives_considered: changing gene order to obtain higher downstream expression - unnecessary because read-through >1 elements exist
Group C short-half-life terminators - reduced both product titers, rejected for production use

experiments.purpose: Apply terminator valve to balance glycolytic growth flux vs myo-inositol (MI) production in two host backgrounds
experiments.host: E. coli MG1655 ΔpfkA Δzwf and E. coli eMS57 ΔpfkA Δzwf (genome-reduced)
experiments.intervention: pMI plasmids: INO1(S. cerevisiae)-[RIT valve]-pfkA(E. coli); 5 valve plasmids tested in ΔpfkA Δzwf hosts; hosts built by sequential lambda-Red knockout (zwf then pfkA)
experiments.conditions: 60 mL M9 high-glucose (10 g/L) + 100 µg/mL amp + 0.1 mM IPTG, OD600 0.05, 300 mL flask, 30°C, up to 48 h, aerobic
experiments.control: conv. sys.: MG1655 wild-type (pfkA, zwf unperturbed) + pTrc-INO1 without valve
experiments.readout: MG1655 ΔpfkA Δzwf optimum at T3PE-383 (read-through 0.519): 0.682 g/L MI, 8.92× conventional system, +38% yield; eMS57 ΔpfkA Δzwf optimum at strong rrnBT: 0.864 g/L (1.27× MG1655 max); unvalved INO1 overexpression caused severe growth retardation and marginal MI
experiments.analysis: HPLC MI + glucose consumption; yield g/g; growth curves (OD-Monitor; Suppl. Fig S9/S10)
experiments.outcome: An intermediate pfkA read-through maximizes MI in MG1655 background; genome-reduced host optimum shifts to strong termination (lower carbon cost of growth); demonstrates host-dependent optimal flux balance findable by valve screening

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: knockout of pfkA/zwf plus INO1-valve-pfkA construct is an active engineering intervention coupling growth to production. Q2 pass: double-knockout strain and pMI series constructed in this study (eMS57 chassis itself from prior work - noted). Q3 pass: identified optimum valve per host and established valve-screening as the optimization method.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking the competing glycolytic route at pfkA (with zwf removed to limit bypass) and reintroducing pfkA under a terminator valve to gate how much carbon re-enters glycolysis vs MI production - competition-node gating with controlled re-supply.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Uncontrolled INO1 overexpression in the ΔpfkA Δzwf background caused severe growth retardation with marginal MI production, showing that hard blocking of glycolysis starves biomass/precursor supply and that a tunable intermediate pfkA level is needed.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured MI titers, glucose consumption, yields and growth across 5 valve strengths in both hosts; pfkA is cited as the effective rate-limiting glycolytic enzyme (ref 54).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit mechanism: production and biomass fluxes are interconnected and constrained by finite cellular resources; gating the rate-limiting glycolytic enzyme at intermediate expression balances resource allocation. Choice of pfkA as the node additionally rests on literature (ref 54).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a heterologous production pathway in E. coli draws on glycolytic carbon and full knockout of the competing glycolytic step (pfkA) causes growth failure, apply a 3'-UTR terminator valve to reintroduce the blocked enzyme at graded expression levels in a ΔpfkA Δzwf background, because an intermediate glycolytic flux balances biomass generation against product flux; the optimal valve strength is host-dependent and must be screened per chassis (validated for myo-inositol production in MG1655 and genome-reduced eMS57 backgrounds).
alternatives_considered: constitutive INO1 overexpression without flux control (conventional pTrc-INO1 system) - severe growth retardation, marginal MI
complete glycolysis block with no pfkA re-expression - growth failure
